ranking_note: wins = lineage Top-10 in the winner's stored run and not in the loser's; gold = edges of the gold universe keys to the patient's reached concepts, hit = the same for the disease the winner ranked at the stored position; graph-only = an edge of the graph the counts are taken from (the winner for gold, hit and base_*, the loser for loser_gold and loser_top10) that the other graph lacks; score share = its part of the 1-hop finding sum (w * idf * n_docs^beta * topic factor, before length normalization and unified evidence); base_* = the same gold counts over all evaluated patients, over those the winner ranks in Top-10, and over those both rank in Top-10; loser_top10 = the ten diseases the loser ranked (all above the gold)

sample_reading.caveat: Claude's own reading of the 30 sampled S-mix-only edges against their sentences and the S-dict diagnostics, not a clinical judgment. One class per edge; likely_wrong is chosen whenever the sentence does not support the edge, whatever the wording.

classes.new_form: paraphrase or implicit wording no dictionary string of the concept matches
classes.dict_should_match: a dictionary string of the concept is in the text; S-dict did not keep it
classes.likely_wrong: the sentence does not support the finding for the disease

rows.note: Lab table row header 'Ionized calcium (mmol/L)' with values; linked to the substance concept calcium ion (T121/T196), no abnormality stated
Table answer cell 'Yes' (registered with a primary care provider) linked to the qualifier value Yes

Cocaine use is named as a cause of secondary tic disorders in adults, not a finding of transient tic disorder (no on-topic document); S-dict matched the same words to another CUI (C3496069 Cocaine use) for this disease
'Epidermal-Nevus syndrome' listed among syndromic causes of noncleft VPI; S-dict matched the same string and named it C5848385 (S-dict has that edge), the phrase table named it C0265329
'premature cardiovascular events' in a case of the disease; the dictionary has 'cardiovascular event' but exact token matching misses the plural
'regional dietary habits' is speculation about ethnic differences, not a finding of acrodermatitis enteropathica; concept is a behaviour (T055) outside the dictionary's semantic types
'reduction of serum ... total protein concentrations' linked to a urine dipstick protein finding; the direction (reduced) is also lost
'bilateral calf tenderness' on examination is a literal phrase, but the UMLS subset the dictionary uses has no string for C0238883 (S-dict extracted only 'tenderness')
'paranoid delusions' in the psychotic-symptom column of a Fahr's disease case table; dictionary string 'paranoid delusion' misses the plural
'non-specific EEG findings' in GAMT deficiency; dictionary string 'eeg finding' misses the plural
'adverse events' is a secondary trial outcome, not a finding of recurrent cellulitis
'liver' as a metastatic site linked to liver extract (T109/T121); the finding would be liver metastasis
Neurotransmitter-deficit table row 'Serotonin | +' linked to the substance serotonin; the reported finding (serotonin deficit) is not what the concept says
'intake of iron supplements' is a trial exclusion criterion
The document is about synovial chondromatosis (Henderson-Jones syndrome), a name collision with Jones syndrome (gingival fibromatosis with deafness); no on-topic document
Lab table row 'FSH | 6.0 mIU/mL (1.0-10)', a normal value, linked to an FSH injectable drug concept (T200)
'evidence of mild motor delay' in a case report; S-dict matched 'mild motor delay' and named it C4314979 (S-dict has that edge), the phrase table named it C0520947
Patient table cell 'Fever, vomiting'; S-dict dropped 'vomiting' because the cue 'normal' from the preceding table cell is within its five-token negation window
Table row 'Growth delay'; S-dict matched it and named it C0151686/C0456070 (S-dict has those edges), the phrase table also named it C0150037
Table cell 'Unknown (PCR)' (Campylobacter species) linked to a vaccine-administration code
Generic skin-tear risk factor table ('prolonged use of chemotherapeutic agents') with no relation to Marsili syndrome; no on-topic document
'marked increased autofluorescence' on imaging is literal, but the UMLS subset the dictionary uses has no string for C4699245 (S-dict extracted only 'increased')
The abbreviation 'FCD' (focal cortical dysplasia) in a table footnote resolved to fleck corneal dystrophy
